summary.one_liner: gtop is a terminal system monitoring dashboard that shows host metrics and a sortable process table.
summary.what_it_does: gtop runs as a full-screen terminal dashboard for watching system resource usage. It is installed as a Node.js package and started with the gtop command. The process table can be sorted by process ID, CPU usage, or memory usage using the p, c, and m keys. Press q (or ctrl+c in most shells) to quit. The README also provides a Docker option that runs it with host networking and host PID namespace so it can read metrics from the host machine. A troubleshooting note covers garbled characters, with a suggested LANG and TERM environment setting.
use_cases: monitor cpu and memory usage in a terminal
check host metrics from a docker container
notable: Sort the process table by PID, CPU, or memory with single keypresses
Docker image that needs host net and pid namespaces to see host metrics
Installs as a global npm command
caveats: Docker use requires host networking and PID namespace sharing
Display may show question marks or odd characters unless locale and TERM variables are set
keywords: see what is using my memory
